result: A plants run builds every mutant with one constant tag and cargo xtask so prints a step: so/<phase> line per phase; Skylake-SP and Zen 1 numbers and two-copy plants data recorded
head: 06d5e7652
informational: Tag linked from an xtask-built object (other option): gain for ordinary dev/CI builds only on edits that change the hash outside boundary's and ld's dependency cone: root-crate mutant 111 -> 48 s (Skylake-SP), 236 -> 86 s (Zen 1 slot); an edit inside the cone gains nothing (boundary rebuilds, 111 / 230 s). Not large, so not a ruling; it would touch D-27.22 and the loader.

Concurrent plants copies win on both hosts: Skylake-SP 12 plants serial 1591 s vs two copies 860 s (copy peak RAM 13.6 and 9.2 GB, serial 19.8 GB); Zen 1 4-core slots, 4 plants serial 1405 s vs two copies 980 s wall (10.3 GB each). Default not changed (needs a --copies option in the tool); recommend default 2 as its own story.
First plants run: pb2-tag-env-not-set SURVIVED because a test run under a plants run inherits that run's tag; fixed by expecting the test process's own tag; final runs 12/12 CAUGHT.

Zen 1 numbers (4-core slot, other tenants load 8-36; before and after trees ran at the same time): cold 868 -> 352 s, no-op 418 -> 60 s, root mutant 704 -> 236 s (86 s with the constant tag), boundary mutant 717 -> 230 s.
